title.narrative: Support to the Amazon Fund, results 2024

description.narrative:
Results-based payment to the Amazon Fund for forest year 2024. The support has been allocated in connection with the 31 per cent reduction in deforestation that Brazil has achieved over the last year. In the period from August 2023 to June 2024, deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon dropped to its lowest level since 2015, and the fifth lowest deforestation rate since measurement began in 1988.
The Amazon Fund’s core mandate is environmental protection through the support of policies focused on the reduction of deforestation and forest degradation, aligned with the PPCDAm and ENREDD+. All supported interventions such as monitoring and control, territorial planning (ZEE), CAR implementation, fire prevention, restoration of degraded areas, and biodiversity conservation directly target environmental outcomes at scale. The Amazon Fund systematically reduces the vulnerability of socio-ecological systems by strengthening forest governance, territorial planning (ZEE), fire prevention, ecosystem restoration, and support to Indigenous Peoples and traditional communities. These interventions increase resilience to climate impacts such as droughts, fires, and ecosystem degradation. Projects supported by the Fund explicitly require participatory governance arrangements, transparency, institutional coordination, and engagement of subnational governments, civil society, Indigenous Peoples, and traditional communities. Gender equality is addressed transversally, particularly in projects targeting Indigenous Peoples, traditional communities, family farmers, and sociobiodiversity value chains. Gender considerations are systematically integrated into implementation and participation requirements.
